book.edition: Carlo Collodi, Le avventure di Pinocchio — De Agostini EPUB (Sigil), Italian, NFC text with accents, « » and curly apostrophes
book.structure: Spine: cover, colophon, frontespizio, indice, pre, Section0001_0001..0036, diz, titoli_collana. NCX (41 entries): Copertina, Colophon, Frontespizio, Capitolo uno..trentasei, Dizionarietto, Indice — so the NCX order differs from the spine (Indice is spine 3 but the last navPoint) and pre.xhtml / titoli_collana.xhtml have no navPoint.

device: Samsung Galaxy S25 (SM-S931B), Android 17, 1080x2340; Moon+ Reader Pro 10.8, automatic Drive sync
display: The user's Moon+ settings (font serif 18.0, line spacing 3, left/right margins 10, top 20, bottom 16), portrait 1080x2340.
notes: Chapter index follows the NCX, not the spine: 'Capitolo uno' is chapter 3 (NCX ordinal 3; spine index 5) and 'Indice' is chapter 40.
Reading order follows the NCX too: Frontespizio (1 page) is followed directly by Capitolo uno; indice.xhtml and pre.xhtml are not shown there.

The last NCX entry, 'Indice', is a chapter of ~130 pages: indice.xhtml, then pre.xhtml, then every chapter again, Dizionarietto and titoli_collana.xhtml to the end of the spine. Its probe 'quel punto fu bussato alla porta.' (Capitolo due's first line) is at 40@0 offset 5578; a naive concatenation of the tag-stripped bodies of indice + pre + Section1 + Section2 puts it at 5577. The status line shows 99.2% while on its page 4.

That merged chapter is split into chunks: the end of the book is 40@2#65889. Concatenating the raw bodies from indice.xhtml on predicts 3 chunks, matching the split index, but the last chunk's naive text is only ~64,026 chars, so Moon+'s assembly of this chapter adds something the plain concatenation doesn't (unknown).

Accented letters (precomposed, NFC), guillemets « », curly apostrophes and '…' count as one character each: every probe in Capitolo uno matches a whitespace-collapsed tag-strip of Section0001_0001.xhtml exactly (14, 127, 138, 506, 552).
Word selection breaks at the curly apostrophe and after a drop cap: long-pressing 'era' after the drop cap 'C’' selected from 'una'.
